claims.text: The initial material is high-purity, single-phase ZrB2 powder.
Conventional ZrB2 sintering requires temperatures above 2300 °C.
The intervention is addition of 3–5 vol% SiC to ZrB2 powder before sintering.
Adding 3–5 vol% SiC will enable ZrB2 densification below 1700 °C.
SiC acts as a reactive sintering aid that enhances mass transport and densification.
High-temperature exposure causes the added SiC to form a continuous intergranular silica or oxy-carbide phase.
The SiC-derived secondary phase reinforces the ZrB2 microstructure.
A SiC-derived silica layer along grain boundaries limits oxygen ingress and oxidation.
The SiC-derived protective phase prevents penetration and corrosion by liquid plating metals.
SiC-doped ZrB2 sintered below 1700 °C will have greater density than both conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
SiC-doped ZrB2 will have superior mechanical integrity relative to both comparison classes.
SiC-doped ZrB2 will have superior high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to both comparison classes.
SiC-doped ZrB2 will have superior liquid plating-metal corrosion resistance relative to both comparison classes.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens without SiC exhibit significant oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion problems.
The proposed service boundary includes oxidation in air up to approximately 1100 °C and exposure to liquid plating metals.
